connections.why: Equilibrium is maintained by energy from fusion
When fuel runs out a star evolves off the main sequence
Low-mass stars end as white dwarfs after shedding envelopes
Massive stars die in core-collapse supernovae
Spectral classes are defined by absorption-line patterns
Spectral type forms the temperature axis of the HR diagram
Evolutionary tracks move stars across the HR diagram
Type Ia supernovae are exploding white dwarfs
Core collapse leaves a neutron star remnant
Above ~3 solar masses, neutron stars collapse into black holes
GR generalises SR to include gravity and acceleration
Event horizons are predictions of GR
GR underpins the FLRW models behind CMB predictions
AGN occupy the central regions of many galaxies
Quasars are powered by accretion onto supermassive black holes
Cluster dynamics provide key evidence for dark matter
The CMB is direct evidence for the hot early universe
Accelerating expansion is explained by dark energy in Big Bang cosmology
Type Ia supernovae standardised distance estimates for cosmology
Detection methods reveal whether planets sit in the habitable zone
Habitable conditions are required for life as we know it
Modern observatories like JWST characterise exoplanet atmospheres
Spectroscopic CCDs record stellar absorption lines
AGN emit strongly across radio, infrared and X-ray bands
